Rationale.Observation: The owner, on 2026-10-07: "we must stay close to agile as SAFe would do it, minimal gates and approvals, needs to be very agile via kanban decision making and tracking at every level"; and "we just need to pick best fitting pieces from all of them to build light process and protocol for each level/layer of our machinery".

The owner, on 2026-10-08: "we have two fundamental floors to everything - the functional, commercial - what needs to be done - the governance, subtle - the institution - the control, policies, risks, etc."; "the governance and assurance layer must not mix with functional it just supports it in some subtle way and it is defined elsewhere and the functional invokes it at proper ways or it is embedded in acceptance or decision making. but not impacting the frictionless functional flow".

The owner on projects: the site defines a project as a project-management (agile) profile and theory, the static part; a live project card, kept in the Portfolio folder and updated outside the site, holds the runtime state (RACI mapping to positions and people, the real Kanban, milestones and deliverables) and is rendered on the live part; "site itself will track the progress over intended project stages but the actual work will be done elsewhere" (Jira); "anything runtime belongs to registry in general. site only holds theory, not live appointments and assignments". The kinds of service need different flows: full machinery (product, project, cross-function, Jira), run-rate (department level, reusable theory, many small projects such as the HR job-description automation), architectural and governance work.

Facts of the corpus on 2026-10-08: nine documents of about 51,000 words, 14 templates, 32 controls, 14 recurring events, a Portfolio Kanban of seven steps with five decision gates and a Pull step, three Steering forums, five Program Increment events in the IP week, a six-section Initiative Brief for every Initiative, a Service Agreement per client function and an Outcome Report. The unit runs in light mode with up to three people.

The 32 controls by type: 17 preventive, 10 detective, 5 directive. By role (first cut of the coordinator, to be reviewed): 6 are functional decisions (C-08 Service Agreement; C-09 approval of the business case and the decision after the MVP; C-10 Outcome Report, acceptance and benefit; C-11 benefit confirmed; C-20 proposal to adopt at scale; C-23 intake and the limit on work in progress); 13 are control points inside the flow (C-12 Risk Tier assignment; C-13 check or validation before the first deployment; C-14 release; C-15 data-class approval and training; C-17 exception, suspension and stop; C-18 check of a provider; C-19 sharing outside the Bank; C-21 published output; C-22 separation of duties and independence; C-27 acceptance of a risk beyond appetite; C-28 reassessment and expiry; C-30 deployment and change; C-31 retirement); 13 run on the governance calendar (C-01 to C-07, C-16, C-24, C-25, C-26, C-29, C-32).

The six research reports of 2026-10-08 (SAFe, other agile methods, PMI and PMO, ITSM, controls for banks and AI, decision methods) agree on seven points: decisions by a pre-agreed rule and one named decider; forums for flow and exceptions, with one monthly forum and the quarterly and yearly reviews inside it; a threshold or guardrail that removes most approvals; an exit criterion, appetite and stop threshold fixed before the work starts; controls in the definition of done scaled to the Risk Tier with the reviewer never the builder; a decision log and a registry as the audit trail; WSJF only as a tie-breaker, with three classes of service. Reliability: SAFe, PMI and ITIL official pages were gated or paywalled, so summaries and practitioner pages were used; one report states that the Federal Reserve letter SR 26-2 superseded SR 11-7 in April 2026, which the coordinator has not checked; the National Bank of the Kyrgyz Republic requirements were not researched.
Rationale.Recommendation: Target model, four levels with one board each. Discover: the catalog and the Funnel list; the Lead decides by rule within a service-level expectation of three working days, and assigns the Risk Tier from a short checklist. Portfolio: Funnel, Shaping, Ready, Doing (MVP, then scale), Done, with limits on work in progress on Shaping and Doing. Program: Backlog, Ready, Active, Review, Done for Capabilities and Features. Team: Jira only.

Three decisions replace five gates and the Pull step. Start (Funnel to Shaping): the Lead, with a Domain Owner named. Invest (Shaping to Ready): the Domain Owner inside the envelope of the Strategic Priority; the Executive Sponsor above the envelope, across Domains, or for enabling work; asynchronous unless someone objects within five days. Persevere, pivot or stop (inside Doing): by the exit criterion, appetite and stop threshold fixed at Invest; a missed threshold means stop or reshape by rule, and the Domain Owner may overrule within five days, logged. Pull is a limit on work in progress; acceptance is part of the definition of done and the benefit is confirmed at the quarterly review.

Classes of service: run-rate, Initiative, and urgent; one urgent item at a time, and urgent never skips a clearance. Mode of work follows Business Model 4.7: run-rate if it fits one Iteration, otherwise an Initiative.

Forums: yearly (envelopes, guardrails, limits, mix, risk appetite), quarterly (review of outcomes against leading indicators, persevere/pivot/stop for running Initiatives, roadmap, and one review-and-plan session for the Program Increment that replaces the five IP-week events), monthly (one 45-minute portfolio forum on flow, aging, blocked items and exceptions, which ratifies the decisions taken asynchronously; the Executive Sponsor receives its decision notes), weekly (program review), monthly Iteration review. Every forum produces log entries with the decision, the decider, the date and a review date.

Two floors. Functional floor: demand, priorities, investment decisions, delivery, acceptance, benefits; first line; owned by the Competence Center Lead and the Domain Owners. Governance floor: policy and risk appetite, Risk Tiers, the control catalogue, control profiles by Tier, registers, assurance and audit; second and third line; owned with the Control Function Contacts, the Executive Sponsor and internal audit. The interface is the control profile by Risk Tier (versioned: which evidence items, from whom, at which hook) and five hooks: Start (Tier assigned), Shaping (clearances requested in parallel), Doing (checks in the definition of done), release and use (release and data-class approval), change (re-tier on a material change). Back to governance: evidence as a by-product, and events such as incidents and exceptions.

Frictionless rules: clearances run in parallel with shaping; a lapsed timebox escalates and never approves, because silence is not consent in a bank; preventive checks only where the Tier demands them, detective sampling otherwise; a card cannot reach Done without the evidence of its profile (a build-time check first, a Jira workflow rule later); governance does not gate items outside the hooks; a change to a profile applies to new items from its effective date; independence is kept by having a reviewer from outside the unit for the higher Tiers.

Project Profiles and Project Cards. A Project Profile is static theory on the site (Program branch): the process, RACI by Role, stages, controls by Tier and the card template. Four kinds first: Initiative delivery; run-rate engagement (the theory of the Standing Initiative and its Features, written once for every department); control activity (tiering, assessments, oversight, on the control calendar); enablement programme. The 15 service categories stay as the catalogue and search fields; the profile carries the process. A Project Card is the live instance, one structured file per project in the Portfolio folder, with at least: identity (id, title, mode, profile and version, stage); people (Roles resolved from the Appointments Record, project-specific roles with position and holder, one named decider and the consulted); outcome (problem, intended outcome, measure with baseline, target and date); constraints (appetite, review date); controls (Tier, data class, profile version, links to clearances and evidence); live state (status, next step, top risks and impediments, dependencies, flow data); work (Capabilities and Features as rows with Jira keys); audit (dated decisions, scope changes, state history); closure (result, benefit check, up to five lessons); links to the Jira epic, board and Confluence.

Folder shape (Portfolio): discovery/ for scenarios (unchanged); profiles/ for the profile theory, card schema and template; initiatives/ with one folder per Initiative named by identifier, holding the card, the Brief and the project documents; run-rate Features as cards under their Standing Initiative. Service area, category, mode, client function and profile are fields. Views by area, category, function and state are generated at build time; a flat export of the cards is built for search and retrieval.

Refactor in phases, each with its own GRACE plan, Decision Record, both editions and passing checks. P0 design: this record and the closing of the open decisions. P1 control mapping: the table of the 32 controls and the first control profiles by Risk Tier, reviewed by the Control Function Contacts. P2 functional flow in the corpus: Portfolio Management Model, Solution Lifecycle Model and Business Model (states, decisions, forums, classes of service, profiles). P3 governance set: the control catalogue and control profiles with the AI Policy and the assurance cadence; the Operating Model reduced to roles and loops. P4 profiles and cards: the four profiles, the card schema and template, validation in the build, the corpus sentence on names and posts. P5 migration: INI-013, the Standing Initiatives and the first run-rate project (HR job descriptions) as cards; backlog and boards generated; the Program views rendered from cards. P6 portal restructure: simpler Center pages around Discover, Decide, Deliver, Do; a later live governance view. P7 later: Jira link fields and, when Jira exists, a status pull.

Alternatives.Alternative: Keep the seven states and five gates with lighter wording: rejected because the cost is in the number of decisions and forums, not in the wording.
Folders per state (funnel/, backlog/) or per service area: rejected, because state and classification change and a path must hold identity so that links and history stay stable.
A card for every Capability and Feature: rejected, because it rebuilds Jira in files; cards exist for a project, and the work items are rows with Jira keys.
Calling the profile a Package: rejected, because Package already names reusable solution kits (PKG-nnn).
Calling the card a passport (паспорт проекта): rejected, because паспорт инициативы is the Initiative Brief.
One flow for all 15 service categories, or a flow per category: rejected in favour of four profiles by kind of work, with the categories as the catalogue.
Full SAFe, with Program Increment planning events, Release Train roles and Participatory Budgeting: rejected for a unit of about three people.

DeferredDecisions.Decision: The Invest threshold: the existing rule (an Initiative is anything beyond one Iteration, with an envelope per Strategic Priority and the Executive Sponsor above it) or an explicit person-weeks figure.
The Executive Sponsor attends only the quarterly and yearly reviews and receives the decision notes of the monthly forum.
The agreement of the Control Function Contacts to a checklist by Risk Tier in place of separate gates.
One Shaping column in place of Reviewing and Analyzing, and the rule-based stop after the MVP with a five-day overrule.
The card file format (YAML checked by a schema, my recommendation, or JSON) and the language of the free text of a card (one language shown as written, or English and Russian pairs).

Whether the live rendering of a card shows positions only or names too; in either case the corpus needs one sentence allowing it (Operating Model 7.4 limits personal data to the names and posts of Holders).
The renaming of the page Journey technical profiles, so that it does not collide with Project Profile; the Russian terms профиль проекта and карточка проекта.
INI-013: show the Domain Owner by a lookup in the Appointments Record; the source scenario of INI-013 in the Discovery catalog.
Requirements of the National Bank of the Kyrgyz Republic and of the Bank on model risk, retention and outsourcing, to be checked with Compliance; the claim about SR 26-2.

Scenarios.Scenario: A department asks for the automation of job descriptions. It matches the run-rate profile, so it enters as a Feature under the Standing Initiative Build and run, with a card; the Lead admits it at the weekly review when a slot is free and the Domain Owner has approved the data class; the card carries the Tier checklist; the requester accepts it; the Program Kanban shows it.

INI-013 is Proposed. The Lead takes it in (Start) and names the Domain Owner by Role; the Control Function Contacts receive the Brief during Shaping and answer within the timebox; the Domain Owner approves inside the envelope (Invest); the MVP runs in the Lab with its exit criterion; at the threshold the Domain Owner persevere, pivot or stop, and the decision is logged. Until the project runs, its card holds no mapping to people.
A Tier 2 Feature has no clearance link on its card. It cannot move to Done in the build check; the quarterly governance sample reads the evidence without touching the flow.
The data class of a live Solution changes. The hook on change triggers a re-tier, the control profile of the new Tier applies, and the registry row is updated.
A card is not touched for longer than its service-level expectation. It appears on the monthly forum list for a stop-or-resume decision; resuming or stopping is logged.
